title: Florida's 12th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Florida's 12th Congressional District is being contested in 2026 following mid-decade redistricting that shifted district boundaries, making the seat more competitive than in previous cycles. Incumbent Republican Rep. Gus Bilirakis, first elected in 2006, is seeking an 11th term and faces a Republican primary challenge from Samantha June. On the Democratic side, former Hillsborough County Commissioner Kimberly Overman is running after switching from the 15th district when redistricting placed her home in CD-12. No-party-affiliation candidate Branden Scrivener is also in the race. The general election is November 3, 2026, with primaries on August 18, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this specific race as of June 2026. The district has historically leaned Republican; under the new map it voted for Trump by 14 points in 2024 according to Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Gus Bilirakis
candidates.summary: Gus Bilirakis is a Republican incumbent representing Florida's 12th Congressional District, first elected in 2006. He serves as a senior member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs the Innovation, Data, and Commerce Subcommittee, and has been rated the most effective Republican member of the Florida congressional delegation by the Center for Effective Lawmaking.

candidates.name: Samantha Elizabeth June
candidates.summary: Samantha Elizabeth June is a Republican candidate challenging incumbent Gus Bilirakis in the August 18 primary for Florida's 12th Congressional District. A graduate of the University of South Florida with a degree in biological health sciences, she advocates for holistic and naturopathic medicine and is an advocate against human trafficking. Her campaign slogan is 'Make Jesus First & Great Again.'

candidates.name: Kimberly Overman
candidates.summary: Kimberly Overman is a Democratic candidate for Florida's 12th Congressional District and a former Hillsborough County Commissioner who served from 2018 to 2022. She switched from running in CD-15 to CD-12 after mid-decade redistricting placed her residence in the newly drawn district. A Certified Financial Planner and former CEO of a fee-only investment advisory firm, her campaign focuses on affordable housing, healthcare access, education, and protecting voting rights.

forecast.rationale: No public polls are available for this race, so the forecast relies on non-polling indicators and carries meaningful uncertainty. The new CD-12 voted for Trump by 14 percentage points in 2024 per Cook Political Report, indicating a continued Republican lean even after mid-decade redistricting made the seat more competitive. Incumbent Gus Bilirakis (first elected 2006) brings strong name recognition, seniority, and a record as the most effective Republican in the Florida delegation. His primary challenger, Samantha June, has limited institutional or fundraising profile and is unlikely to alter the general-election outlook. Democrat Kimberly Overman is a credible candidate — a former Hillsborough County Commissioner — but faces an uphill climb in a district with a double-digit Republican baseline. An NPA candidate (Branden Scrivener) is also on the ballot but has no significant campaign infrastructure evident. Given the partisan baseline and incumbency advantage, Republicans remain clear favorites, but the absence of polling and the redrawn boundaries keep this in the 'likely' rather than 'safe' category.
